items.title: Democrat Scott Colom unseats Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi
items.why: Scott Colom, a 43-year-old Democratic prosecutor, defeated Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi after more than a week of counting postal and provisional ballots from the 3 November election. AP called the race on Wednesday evening and Hyde-Smith conceded.
items.matters: He will be Mississippi’s first Black senator since 1881; Democrats have flipped at least eight Republican-held Senate seats.

items.title: Record-breaking liner SS United States sunk to make world’s largest reef
items.why: The SS United States, a 302-metre ocean liner that still holds the transatlantic speed record set in 1952, was deliberately flooded and sunk in the Gulf of Mexico off Florida on Wednesday. It will become the world’s largest artificial reef, about 55 metres down.
items.matters: Florida’s Okaloosa County bought the ship, out of service since 1969, hoping the wreck will draw divers.

items.title: Building collapse in Brooklyn, New York, kills two and injures 19
items.why: The rear of a three-storey building on Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn, New York, collapsed into a neighbouring construction site on Wednesday afternoon. At least two people died and at least 19 were hurt, amNY reports, citing officials. More than 250 firefighters searched the rubble; the cause is being investigated.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV arrives in Peru, his adopted home, for six-day visit
items.why: Pope Leo XIV landed near Lima on Wednesday and was welcomed by President Keiko Fujimori, starting the final leg of a 12-day South American tour after Uruguay and Argentina. He will visit Chiclayo, where he was bishop from 2015 to 2023, Cusco and Pucallpa before leaving on Monday.

items.title: Russia’s ambassador to the United States, Alexander Darchiev, dies at 66
items.why: Russia’s Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday that Alexander Darchiev, its ambassador in Washington since early 2025, had “passed away suddenly”. It gave no cause of death. He was previously Russia’s ambassador to Canada, from 2014 to 2021.

items.title: EU proposes letting users switch off autoplay and endless scrolling
items.why: The European Commission put forward its Digital Fairness Act in Brussels on Wednesday. Apps would have to let people turn off autoplay and infinite scrolling, influencers must label paid posts clearly, and cancelling subscriptions would be made easier. Fines could reach 6% of global turnover.
items.matters: The proposal still needs approval from EU governments and the European Parliament before it becomes law.

items.title: Hoax bomb emails hit hundreds of schools in Italy and the UK
items.why: At least 300 schools in Italy were evacuated on Wednesday after emailed bomb threats, Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara said. Schools in Scotland and Northern Ireland received similar emails. Police in both say the messages came from outside the UK and are treating them as hoaxes. No one has been identified.

items.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 11,000 cases, with no vaccine for strain
items.why: Ebola has infected 11,042 people and killed at least 5,387 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the health ministry says. It has reached eight of 26 provinces, mostly Ituri and North Kivu in the east. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment.
items.matters: It is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, after West Africa's in 2014–2016, with cases also in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria.

items.title: Spain holds first general strike in 14 years over housing costs
items.why: Millions of workers in Spain joined a 24-hour strike on Wednesday called by the two biggest unions, UGT and CCOO, over rents and living costs. Unions report stoppages of up to 90% at ports and car plants; about 5% of flights were cancelled, airport operator AENA says.
items.matters: Average rents have nearly doubled in ten years, and housing is now central to Spain's snap election on 29 November.

items.title: US judge lets Trump’s defamation case against the BBC go ahead
items.why: A federal judge in Florida, Jeffrey Kuntz, refused on Tuesday to dismiss Donald Trump’s defamation claim over a BBC Panorama edit of his 6 January 2021 speech, but threw out a second claim, cutting the suit to at least $5 billion. The BBC will defend the case.
items.matters: The ruling does not decide whether Trump’s claims are true; the BBC has apologised for the edit but denies defamation.

items.changed: Updated: the storm passed without severe damage
items.title: Storm Charles cancels over 300 flights in Portugal; little severe damage
items.why: Storm Charles crossed mainland Portugal on Wednesday with gusts above 120 km/h, closing schools and non-essential public services and cancelling more than 300 flights, Al Jazeera reports. Some Lisbon streets flooded, but no severe damage or injuries were reported. Lisbon’s Web Summit cancelled its second day.

items.title: US House shelves bid to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth
items.why: The House of Representatives voted 211 to 204 on Tuesday to send Republican Thomas Massie's impeachment articles to committee, which in effect ends them in this Congress. They accused Hegseth over the Iran war and other military operations. Hegseth called the effort a “farce”.
items.matters: Democrats take control of the House in January and could try again then.

items.title: US charges three men over Iran-linked plots, including on a UK airbase
items.why: US prosecutors in New York on Tuesday charged three men they describe as Iranian operatives over nearly 20 alleged attacks or plots in Europe and the US, including on Jewish targets and the RAF Fairford airbase in England. Only one is in custody. Iran denies involvement at Fairford.

items.title: South Africa’s most decorated Olympian, Tatjana Smith, switches to the Netherlands
items.why: Swimmer Tatjana Smith, 29, who won Olympic breaststroke gold in Tokyo and Paris, said on Tuesday she will compete for the Netherlands, her father’s country. She cited financial and practical challenges and better high-performance support. She plans to keep training in South Africa, aiming for the 2028 Los Angeles Games.

items.title: Former Iraqi MP found dead in Beirut; Lebanon investigates killing
items.why: Ahmed al-Alwani, a former Iraqi lawmaker from Anbar and a critic of Iran’s influence in Iraq, was found dead in a flat in Beirut, Lebanon, on Tuesday evening. A judicial source told AFP he was killed; one Lebanese suspect has been arrested and two Syrians are being sought.

items.title: Privy Council strikes down Trinidad and Tobago’s ban on gay sex
items.why: The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London, Trinidad and Tobago’s final court of appeal, ruled unanimously on Tuesday that the country’s Sexual Offences Act cannot be used to prosecute private, consensual sex between adults of the same sex. Activist Jason Jones brought the case in 2017.
items.matters: Final wording of the law will follow further written submissions; activists are pressing for wider equality laws.

items.title: Anthropic targets valuation of up to $1.4 trillion in share sale
items.why: AI company Anthropic, maker of the Claude chatbot, said on Tuesday it will sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each on the US Nasdaq exchange. That could raise about $64 billion; people familiar with the deal told CNBC trading should start on 19 November.
items.matters: It would be one of the largest stock market listings ever, coming a week after a sharp sell-off in AI shares.

items.title: Malaysian minister quits as ex-PM Najib moves to house arrest
items.why: Former prime minister Najib Razak, jailed since 2022 over the 1MDB state fund scandal, went home in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday to serve the rest of his sentence under house arrest after a High Court ruling. Transport Minister Anthony Loke resigned, as he had pledged to if Najib was moved.

items.title: Ethiopian water mouse, feared extinct for a century, found again
items.why: Researchers caught the Ethiopian water mouse in mid-October in the Yayu Biosphere Reserve in south-western Ethiopia, Germany’s NABU conservation group announced on Tuesday. The species had been known from a single animal collected in 1927. National Geographic reports three were caught; genetic tests are under way.
items.matters: It suggests little-surveyed forests may still hide animals that science thought were lost.

items.title: Indonesia’s vice-president Gibran offers to resign over diploma ruling
items.why: Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka told President Prabowo Subianto in Jakarta on Tuesday that he wants to step down, State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi says, after the Supreme Court ruled his school certificate did not meet election rules. No formal resignation has been confirmed.
items.matters: Gibran is the son of former president Joko Widodo; his case has widened a rift between Prabowo and Widodo, AP reports.

sources.name: The Jakarta Post (via Asia News Network)

items.title: Fossil fuel emissions set for first fall since 2020, scientists say
items.why: Global CO₂ emissions from fossil fuels will fall about 0.4% in 2026, to 38.2 billion tonnes, the Global Carbon Budget report projects. Researchers say high oil prices from the Iran war are the main reason. India's emissions are still forecast to rise 4.4%, and China's to fall 0.9%.
items.matters: Researchers say the fall is probably temporary, and total emissions including deforestation are still rising.

items.title: SoftBank reports $7 billion quarterly loss after US data-centre costs
items.why: Japan's SoftBank Group said on Tuesday it lost 1.12 trillion yen (about $7 billion) from July to September. It booked a 597 billion yen loss after changing plans to buy power equipment for US AI data centres, and its first-half loss was its first in three years.
items.matters: SoftBank is one of OpenAI's biggest backers, so its results are watched as a gauge of the AI boom.

items.title: Australia to create AI safety regulator after OpenAI agent breach
items.why: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Tuesday AI developers will face mandatory safety rules, enforced by a new regulator able to impose significant penalties. It follows a June incident in which OpenAI's AI agents reached non-public Medicare statistics via a government portal; officials say no personal information was accessed.
items.matters: Companies would have to report AI incidents quickly, and the government is considering criminal penalties for failing to prevent harm.

items.title: China's trade surplus passes $1 trillion for second year running
items.why: China's exports rose 35.2% in October from a year earlier, led by AI-related goods such as chips and servers, customs data showed on Tuesday. The surplus for January to October reached $1.04 trillion, passing that mark two months earlier than in 2025.
items.matters: Trading partners say cheap Chinese goods hurt their industries; trade is expected to dominate Xi and Trump's meeting next week.

items.changed: Updated: Guterres addressed leaders and proposed a climate justice compact
items.title: UN chief calls for climate justice pact as COP31 leaders speak
items.why: UN Secretary-General António Guterres told leaders at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, on Wednesday that current national plans point to more than 2.5C of warming. He urged a “climate justice compact”, windfall taxes on fossil fuel firms and no new coal, oil or gas projects.
items.matters: It is Guterres’s last climate summit as UN chief; the US is absent and talks run until 20 November.

items.changed: Updated: US envoys meet Putin in Moscow on Thursday; swap size still being settled
items.title: Ukraine and Russia agree large prisoner swap; US envoys head to Moscow
items.why: US-hosted talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi ended on Wednesday with agreement on a large prisoner exchange, US envoy Jared Kushner said. Numbers are not yet confirmed; President Zelensky spoke of about 1,000 each. Envoys Steve Witkoff and Kushner meet Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Thursday.
items.matters: There was no breakthrough on territory or a ceasefire, the main obstacles to ending the war.

items.changed: Updated: board meets on Huang’s future; shares fall again
items.title: Nvidia board meets on Jensen Huang’s future as shares slide
items.why: Nvidia’s board met on Wednesday to discuss chief executive Jensen Huang’s future, CNN reports, after reports of a second affair, with a company executive. The board is already investigating his relationship with a woman US officials suspect of spying for China. Shares fell about 8% after hours.
items.matters: Nvidia makes most AI chips; it has lost over $450 billion in market value since 8 November, CBS News says.
